output.metric: One channel's signups flatlined at zero
output.observed_change: Signups attributed to the affiliate channel dropped to zero on the 14th and have stayed there for 22 days.
output.notes: A competitor launched a campaign in the same week. Overall site traffic genuinely dipped 4 percent.

blind_spots: marts.signups has NO owners recorded in DataHub (ownership returned an empty owner set) — a finding, not a clean result: no one is accountable and there is no one to route this incident to.

marts.signups returned 0 schema fields from DataHub (totalFields=0) — column-level structure of the metric is unknown from metadata; the view SQL (via warehouse.schema) has not been read, so any channel-bucketing or filtering rule inside the metric definition is unmapped.

staging.events_daily is described as bucketing on LOCAL TIME — the timezone/day-boundary rule lives in the view text, not in metadata; this is a known blind spot to inspect before trusting per-day, per-channel counts.
raw.web_sessions carries an is_automated flag that 'not every producer sets' — bot/automation filtering is inconsistent at the source; how nulls are treated downstream is unknown.

raw.channel_events_raw is 'written by per-channel collectors' — the affiliate channel is served by its own collector, so a single-collector fault would zero exactly one channel while others continue; collector health is not represented in DataHub metadata.

No schema fields are recorded in DataHub for staging.events_daily, raw.channel_events_raw, or raw.web_sessions — only prose descriptions are available; column coverage across the whole path is a metadata blind spot.

Every dataset on the path reports INCIDENTS health = PASS despite a real 22-day flatline at zero — either no assertion covers per-channel signup volume or assertions are not wired to this metric; absence of a failing assertion here is not absence of fault.

tool_calls.ref: search:affiliate channel signups by channel daily

output.statement: The affiliate channel's own per-channel collector stopped writing rows to raw.channel_events_raw on day 14, so the measurement path reports zero affiliate signups while affiliate-driven signups actually continued at roughly their prior rate.
would_be_confirmed_by: raw.channel_events_raw shows a hard step to zero affiliate-channel rows on day 14 that persists through day 36, while every other channel's daily row count continues normally
the affiliate collector's process health or ingestion logs show a halt, crash, or credential/endpoint failure dated on or about day 14
the drop is a single-step flatline to exactly zero rather than a gradual decline
signups for all non-affiliate channels in marts.signups are unaffected across days 14-36
would_be_refuted_by: raw.channel_events_raw contains affiliate-channel rows for days 14-36 at roughly the pre-day-14 volume (source data is arriving, so no collector outage — fault is downstream or definitional)
affiliate signups declined gradually across the window instead of dropping to exactly zero in one step
two or more channels zeroed out simultaneously on day 14 (a single per-channel collector fault cannot zero multiple independent collectors)
the affiliate collector's health check or write logs show it running and successfully committing rows throughout days 14-36

output.statement: The affiliate channel's actual signups genuinely fell to near-zero starting day 14 because the competitor's same-week campaign captured the affiliate partners' audience; the measurement path is working correctly and the zero is a true count of real user behaviour.
would_be_confirmed_by: Independent upstream sources also drop to ~zero on day 14: affiliate rows from the per-channel collector in raw.channel_events_raw AND affiliate-referred sessions in raw.web_sessions both collapse together, so the loss is present before the mart, not introduced by it.
External affiliate-partner referral / payout logs show affiliate-driven visits and conversions collapsing in the same week.
The decline has a behavioural profile (decay or a competitor-correlated dip) and other channels also softened consistent with the observed 4 percent traffic drop.
would_be_refuted_by: Upstream affiliate activity continued at roughly its prior volume after day 14 — affiliate rows still arriving in raw.channel_events_raw and/or affiliate-referred sessions still present in raw.web_sessions — while only the signup count reads zero, locating the loss in the measurement path rather than in users.

The series is an exact step to zero on a single day and pinned at exactly zero for 22 consecutive days rather than a decay or noisy near-zero; organic behaviour rarely produces an exact-zero cliff, whereas a broken or definitional cutoff does.
Affiliate-partner or external referral logs show affiliate clicks and conversions continuing after day 14.
The competitor campaign ended or overall traffic recovered from the 4 percent dip, yet affiliate signups stayed pinned at zero — genuine behaviour would have rebounded, a stuck zero would not.

output.statement: On day 14 the channel-attribution rule that defines the affiliate segment inside marts.signups (or its upstream staging.events_daily) was deliberately changed — the affiliate bucket's matching predicate was renamed, merged, or re-scoped — so real and still-continuing affiliate signups are now attributed to a different channel label, and the affiliate metric reads zero because the metric's meaning changed, not because the underlying count did.
would_be_confirmed_by: A dbt model change, PR, or config/taxonomy edit touching the affiliate channel's attribution predicate or the channel-bucketing CASE/WHEN in marts.signups or staging.events_daily is dated on or around day 14.
Another channel bucket (e.g. 'partner', 'direct', 'unknown', 'other') shows a step increase of roughly the affiliate channel's prior daily volume starting exactly on day 14.
Applying the pre-day-14 channel-bucketing definition to post-day-14 raw data recovers nonzero affiliate signups from events that are present in raw.channel_events_raw.
would_be_refuted_by: The view/model SQL for marts.signups and staging.events_daily shows no edit to the channel-bucketing or attribution logic (CASE/WHEN, WHERE, channel-mapping) in the window around day 14 — the dbt model version/git history is unchanged.
Re-running the current metric definition over pre-day-14 data still yields the historical nonzero affiliate counts (the same rule reproduces the old numbers, so the definition did not change).

raw.channel_events_raw contains no affiliate-labelled events from day 14 onward — the events are absent at the source, so there is nothing being re-attributed (points to a missing-rows instrument fault, not a redefinition).

Total signups across all channels fell by approximately the affiliate channel's lost volume on day 14, with no other channel's count rising to absorb it (consistent with a real disappearance rather than re-attribution).

output.narrative: The signups metric is a pure pass-through: an affiliate signup count is exactly the number of affiliate rows in channel_events_raw for that day, with no channel-remapping CASE/WHEN, WHERE filter, or independent user-behaviour input (e11, e21, e22). In channel_events_raw the affiliate per-channel collector's output stops dead at the day-13/14 boundary (last row 2026-06-13) while the organic, paid_social and referral collectors all keep writing normally through day 36 (e12, e25) — the source rows are simply missing from day 14 on. An instrument independent of that collector, raw.web_sessions, shows affiliate-referred human demand did NOT collapse: ~61 sessions/day both before and after day 14, all human, flat across the boundary with no dip (e13). The signup series is therefore an exact-zero cliff, dropping from ~21/day to entirely absent in a single day and pinned there for 22 days — the broken/definitional signature, not the decay or noisy near-zero of genuine behaviour (e14). This is a measurement failure: the affiliate collector halted on day 14 while real affiliate users kept arriving, so the metric reads zero because the instrument stopped, not because customers left.
